items.question: The values 4, 16, 30, 20, 10, 14 and 26 are represented on a pie chart. Find the sum of the sector angles for values greater than or equal to 16.
items.explanation: The values total 120. Those at least 16 are 16, 30, 20 and 26, totalling 92. Their share of the full circle is (92/120)×360°=276°.
items.observed_question: 4, 16, 30, 20, 10, 14 and 26 are represented on a pie chart. Find the sum of the angles of the bisectors representing all numbers equals to or greater than 16

per_option_reasoning.A: 48° would represent16/120 of the circle, not all qualifying values.

items.question: A car travels P km from Calabar to Enugu at an average speed of U km/h, then Q km to Benin at an average speed of W km/h. Find its average speed for the complete journey.
items.explanation: Average speed is total distance divided by total time. The two journey times are P/U and Q/W hours, so the average is (P+Q)/(P/U+Q/W)=UW(P+Q)/(PW+QU).
items.observed_question: A car travels from calabar to Enugu, a distance of P km with an average speed of U km per hour and continues to benin, a distance of Q km, with an average speed of Wkm per hour. Find its average speed from Calabar to Benin

per_option_reasoning.A: Missing UW numerator factor after bringing the two times to a common denominator.
per_option_reasoning.B: Total distance/(P/U+Q/W) simplifies to this expression.
per_option_reasoning.C: Omits the second leg time QU in the denominator.
per_option_reasoning.D: Omits total distance P+Q from the numerator.

items.question: If g(x)=x²+3x, find g(x+1)−g(x).
items.explanation: Substitute x+1: g(x+1)=(x+1)²+3(x+1)=x²+5x+4. Subtract x²+3x to obtain 2x+4=2(x+2).
items.observed_question: If g(x) = x\(^2\) + 3x  find g(x + 1) - g(x)

per_option_reasoning.C: Accounts for the square term change but omits the additional 3 from 3(x+1).
per_option_reasoning.D: The quadratic term cancels; x²+4 cannot be the difference.

items.question: For real x, determine the maximum value of y=3x²+5x−3.
items.explanation: The coefficient of x² is positive, so the parabola opens upwards and y grows without bound as |x| increases. It has a minimum, y=3(x+5/6)²−61/12, but no finite maximum; none of the numerical options is a maximum.
